select t.table_schema, t.table_name
from information_schema.tables t
where t.table_type = 'BASE TABLE'
  and t.table_schema not in ('auth','storage','realtime','vault','extensions','cron','net',
        'pgsodium','graphql','graphql_public','_analytics','supabase_functions',
        'supabase_migrations','pgbouncer','deprecated','graveyard','pg_catalog','information_schema')
  and not exists (select 1 from pg_inherits i
                  where i.inhrelid = format('%I.%I', t.table_schema, t.table_name)::regclass)

unregistered_derivation.note: An unregistered base table has no registry value, so its type is read off what is ENFORCED on it: grants, RLS policy quals, triggers, primary keys and foreign keys. Rules are evaluated in this order, first match wins. Never by name, with the single exception of R1, which CUT-14 states verbatim as a name rule.

rules.R1: name matches CUT-14's backup/temp rule (_bak_*, _backup*, *_backup_<date>, _stage_*, dated one-off repair artefact) -> Deprecated
rules.R2: an append-only trigger that raises unconditionally on UPDATE and/or DELETE -> Ledger
rules.R2g: no role holds UPDATE or DELETE while INSERT and SELECT are granted - append-only enforced by grant -> Ledger
rules.R3: no SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grant to anon, authenticated or service_role - unreachable by any API principal -> System
rules.R4s: service_role is the only grantee AND the table sits in a platform-machinery schema (platform, iam, public migration plumbing) -> System (Doctrine §1.1 names the registry, iam and meta plumbing under System). A service-role-only table in a FEATURE schema would be Restricted.
rules.R5: a SELECT policy whose qual is `true` for authenticated, with no client write arm - public-readable, platform-owned, never user-created -> Reference
rules.R6: every read arm resolves through a parent RECORD's access (EXISTS over the parent, parent_id IN readable_*(), iam.has_access on the parent, a primary key that IS the parent key, or a junction primary key) -> Detail
rules.R7: a read arm on the table's OWN organization_id, owner_id or auth.uid() -> Entity
rules.R7a: its own organization_id with an org-stamping trigger (_stamp_org_default / stamp_run_org / _inherit_org), but only an is_platform_admin() policy arm because the table never passed through iam.apply_rls -> Entity
rules.R8: the only policy arm is is_platform_admin() (or is_admin/is_super_admin/service_role) and there is no organization_id, no owner_id and no parent record -> System
rules.R8a: a platform-ingested catalog: no organization_id, no owner_id, no parent record, and its only writer is a platform ingest path -> Reference
rules.R9: no client read arm at all, no org-stamping, and writes arrive only through SECURITY DEFINER code -> System

findings_for_W1_REG: CUT-14's exclusion list names a schema that does not exist (`deprecated`) and omits the one that does (`graveyard`). Verbatim the universe is 962, not 956.

All 21 is_active=false registry rows are among the 24 that point at nothing, which is why the registered-and-backed half contains zero Deprecated rows. Deprecated in this census comes entirely from the 7 unregistered backup/stage/dated-repair tables.

Four registry rows point at a relation that no longer exists anywhere and are NOT in the graveyard schema: platform.org_knob_override, platform.user_knob_override, public.agent_user_kv, user.profiles. These are the four the BUILD-BOOK told this lane to investigate; none can be re-pointed.
Three registry rows point at VIEWS (agent.card, content_ir.kind_conformance, workflow.card) and all three carry audit_class='machinery'. Doctrine §1.1: views take no type.

Eight tables are enforced as world-readable platform data (a SELECT policy with qual `true` for authenticated) that are not catalogs: platform.mtx_media_heal_queue, scraper.scrape_failure_log, scraper.scrape_retry_queue, scraper.scrape_path_override, scraper.scrape_domain_settings, scraper.scrape_domain, scraper.scrape_path_pattern, ops.ops_issue_class. They are typed Reference because that is what is enforced; if that is wrong the fix is a policy, not a type.
research.research_intent has RLS DISABLED while `authenticated` holds SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE - every signed-in principal can read and rewrite every row.

About forty unregistered tables carry full table grants to `authenticated` while their only policy arm is is_platform_admin(). They are not broken, they are ungenerated: they never passed through iam.apply_rls. Registering them is what turns the admin-only arm into the type's own policy.
campaign_watch.build_lock is the campaign's own object and is unclassified on production today; registering it as System takes the campaign-scoped unclassified count to zero.
